selectedFirstPrototype.reason: The three real cases have small, exact allowedInputFiles and the first B/D question is authorization judgment/evidence/coverage honesty, not active repository discovery. Embedding the complete allowed bytes removes tool-policy and search-recall confounds.
explicitlyNotTested: model access to the internet or target network
flow: host parses the case manifest outside the model workspace
host creates a fresh isolated work directory and verifies every exact allowedInputFile
host reads only those files and renders B organized instructions or D canonical declaration/support with identical task facts
host sends the full bounded context through a structured provider call with no model tools
host validates structure and evidence references, stores result/trace/evaluation outside the model-visible directory, and never copies oracle/fix/advisory bytes into the run

laterDiscoveryExperiment.question: Can the agent enumerate and map sibling authorization entries within a predeclared repository/path boundary, including the hidden process_file omission?
laterDiscoveryExperiment.separationReason: Adding search tools and larger source changes the intervention and should not be mixed into the first judgment comparison.
enforcement: canonicalize every requested path and reject it unless it is an exact allowlist member or within an explicitly allowed source root
reject absolute paths, parent traversal, symlink escapes, unknown tool names, writes, commands, subprocesses, web/network, and target execution
bound returned bytes/results and record query/path/duration
keep oracle and evaluator files outside every readable root

reusableExistingComponents.use: Load or construct public skill instructions only. Never locate the research cases/oracles inside a loaded skill directory because loadSkill recursively includes bundle files.

Reuse run identity, fresh workdir, snapshots/manifests, adapter lifecycle, and result capture only after generating an isolated task/fixture directory containing exactly allowed files. copyTaskFixtures recursively copies a sibling fixtures directory, so pointing it at the cases parent would leak evaluator data.

Reuse Zod-validated structured output for the no-tool fixed-context path, with targeted telemetry wrapping because an initial failed tool-use response is not included in the returned fallback token/cost aggregate.
Later restricted-read mode can supply a narrow tool array and rejecting executor while reusing multi-turn dispatch, token/cost accumulation, tool-call trace, timeout, and callbacks.
Do not use unchanged for a source-only run. It always registers read/write/command/list/web tools and delegates to executors not designed as a strict read allowlist.

currentUnsafeForSourceOnly: BareAgentAdapter passes AGENT_TOOLS plus list_directory and web_fetch on every run; AGENT_TOOLS includes write_file and execute_command.
createAgentToolExecutor resolves read/write paths against workDir but does not reject paths that escape it; list_directory has the same issue.
execute_command inherits the host environment and web_fetch can reach arbitrary URLs, subject only to ordinary runtime behavior.
A prompt saying source-only/no-network cannot remove these host capabilities.
loadSkill and executeRun deploy all non-excluded bundle files; an oracle stored beside public skill content would be exposed.
hostResponsibilities: accept and verify repository ref, case ID, exact allowed inputs, and B/D condition
create/copy only the isolated model-visible bytes and keep evaluator state elsewhere
render identical task facts for B and D and retain the normalized D declaration
enforce zero tools for fixed context or a strict read allowlist for discovery
validate result structure/evidence locations, run semantic evaluation, and write artifacts after the model call
separate model-provider network from model/agent target-network capability
record every generation, fallback, format repair, domain repair, and tool action with its own usage/status

metering.generation: Count the initial semantic response call(s) and their provider usage/cost.
metering.structuredTransportFallback: Count a failed forced tool-use transport and prompt+parse attempts separately; this is transport recovery, not domain repair.
metering.formatRepair: Count schema/JSON correction separately and do not change domain evidence requirements.
metering.domainRepair: Only a post-validation call using actionable authorization evidence; if the formal comparison allows one, both arms receive the same budget and it is reported separately.
metering.tools: For later discovery, record tool name, allowed path/query, duration, result size, rejection, and model tokens surrounding the calls.
metering.cost: Preserve actual provider USD only when available; estimated cost and unknown USD are distinct. AgentLoop totalCostUsd is all-or-nothing across responses, while BareAgent RunResult.cost may be estimated.

knownTelemetryGap.issue: When tool-use produces a response but then fails content/schema handling and extractStructured falls back to prompt+parse, the returned fallback tokens/cost do not include the failed tool-use response. Prompt+parse retries do aggregate among themselves.
knownTelemetryGap.minimalFutureAction: Wrap the provider/call path with per-attempt telemetry or add a focused aggregation change and test before reporting B/D total usage; do not refactor the whole provider subsystem in this research round.

failureOwnership: provider/auth/rate-limit failure is infrastructure and not a task-quality error
parse/schema failure is structured-transport or format failure
domain validation failure is task-result quality and may receive only the predeclared equal repair opportunity
tool denial/path escape is host-policy enforcement and must be retained, not retried through a broader tool
timeout/max-iteration status is operational outcome and never silently scored as a correct answer
